content.comment_body: Hello, I have several 4-20 mA transmitters with local displays, allowing me to view the range and measured values. However, after numerous attempts, I still cannot obtain accurate readings in [product_name]. Transmitter one: calibrated range 4-20 mA for 0-100°C (when forcing 4 mA, it outputs 3.28 mA instead). Transmitter two: calibrated range 5-20 mA for 0-100°C. Transmitter three: calibrated range 4-20 mA for -29 to 80°C. For wiring, the 24VDC positive is connected to the transmitter’s + terminal and the negative is connected to I1 in [product_name] analog module. I have reviewed all relevant forum discussions and information here, but still don’t understand how to configure gain and offset (min/max) values. There is always a difference in readings of 1.5 to 5 degrees compared to the transmitter display. I tested each transmitter individually. Can you please advise what steps I should take? Thank you.
Please specify the manufacturer and the model of the transmitters.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faces recurring calibration issues with several 4-20 mA temperature transmitters connected to an analog input module in [product_name]. After consulting available documentation and discussions, they still cannot properly set the gain and offset, which results in consistent discrepancies of 1.5 to 5 degrees between the readings and the transmitter display. The issue persists across different transmitter models despite individual troubleshooting efforts.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the analog module in [product_name] to deliver temperature readings that match the transmitters’ local displays after proper configuration. They seek clear instructions for setting the gain and offset parameters for analog input, aiming for reliable and accurate integration.
